title: Ottawa commits $1.6B to Cohere for sovereign AI: what it means for Canadian data control
post:
Your customers are starting to send AI tools to your business. Is your website ready to talk to them, or will it turn away potential sales?

Ottawa is investing big in Canadian AI for a clear reason: to keep your sensitive data here. This is good news if you're worried about client privacy, especially with Quebec's Law 25.

But there's a flip side. Major Canadian banks are now blocking certain AI tools from touching customer data. That's a huge signal for any small business using AI for quotes, customer emails, or client records.

And it's not just privacy. Hackers are actively targeting AI platforms. If your team uses a low-cost AI plan for daily tasks, you need to know what data it's accessing and how secure it is. The cost of not checking could be significant.

Finally, think about your online presence. My analytics show that your customers are increasingly using personal AI agents to compare prices and navigate websites. If your site isn't built to talk to these 'machine visitors,' you might be losing business without knowing it.

This means adapting isn't just about saving your team time. It's about being ready for how customers will interact with you next.

What's one thing your team uses AI for right now where you know you could be getting more value, but haven't had time to dig in?

#SmallBusiness #AIforBusiness #CanadianBusiness #Privacy #Productivity
